acceptance.item: P6-RT-08-04: Attack 30 (a), sibling of P5-RT-08-01: the Atlas writes 'the fundamental weight ω_i' in its sentences and link texts, where the site's word is the fundamental position e_i
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/atlas.test.ts > regressions > the Atlas writes the fundamental weight omega_i where the site writes e_i > AtlasSheet.astro: no omega_i and no "fundamental weight" in the sentences of the sheet (and > atlasData.ts: no "fundamental weight" or "the weight of node" in the link texts); site/tests/e2e/T14.spec.ts > regressions > no Atlas page writes the fundamental weight omega_i where the site writes the fundamental position e_i
acceptance.evidence: Severity minor as filed, raised to major by the reproduce verifier. Red at base 0436a53: the unit tests 2 failed (2) and listed AtlasSheet.astro:236 and :258, atlasData.ts:341 and :347, as observed; the browser test failed on A1 ('from the fundamental weight of node 1', 'Orbits of the fundamental weights', 'The orbit of the fundamental weight ωi'). Green: atlas.test.ts plus atlas-build-path.test.ts 126 passed; T14.spec.ts 31 passed. Cause: the sheet and two link texts used the Lie theory name where SPEC Appendix C and 8.4 bullet 2 give 'fundamental position e_i', as RT-FIX-P5-t12-content already applied to T12. The minuscule and orbit sentences and the minus-w0 and orbit-sizes links now write the fundamental position (the end of the minus-w0 link too: 'minus the fundamental position of node k'), and the opening paragraph defines e_i once. The heading was decided by the same rule ('Orbits of the fundamental positions') and recorded in the fragment. Commit 2c6e0b9.

acceptance.evidence: Severity major (no adjustment). Red on the base build: the script reproducer printed '32 Atlas pages show a population with its numbers and lack the sentence of 2.4(a)' (exit 1), and the adopted test failed with lacking = A1 to G2 (32 boards). Green on the fixed build: script '0 Atlas pages ...' (exit 0); test passed (all 32 pages; [data-bridge] once, text exactly 'The number on node i is the amount by which a mutation would lower city i.'). Cause: AtlasSheet.astro shows θ beside Cθ, the highest short root with its numbers and a = Cp, but never printed the [D] sentence. Each sheet now prints it once, word for word, after the opening paragraph. That paragraph gains 'The translator sends a population p to the numbers a = Cp, and a mutation at node i replaces p_i by p_i - a_i'. The letters i are inline MathML, as T9 sets them. The pages still ship no script (size 0.0 kB). Commit 9e815b9.

handoff: Every changed file is inside the cluster (components/atlas, the T14 tests, the fragment); the registry and pages/atlas are unchanged, and no data-out name was added (the new hook is data-bridge, listed at the top of T14.spec.ts). The proposedFix of P6-RT-10-02 asks for 'the letters set as mathematics'. KaTeX's htmlAndMathml output doubles each letter and fails the reproducer's pattern, so the i is inline MathML (T9's form), and the derivation 'a mutation at node i replaces p_i by p_i - a_i' sits in the paragraph before it instead of a provenance line, so the provenance list of T14.spec.ts is unchanged. On P6-RT-08-04 the heading 'Orbits of the fundamental weights' was changed to 'Orbits of the fundamental positions' by the same rule, replacing that title in decisions/P6-A4.md 'the items as shown'; the sheet gives no Lie theory name for the term, because the adopted reproducer forbids omega_i in its sentences and the Atlas has no Lie theory paragraph. The lens may want to look at the Lie theory words that stay in the opening paragraph ('simple roots', 'Dynkin labels'), which no finding names.
